brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Four full hex bases: (0,0) and (1,0) on level 0 and on level 1, joined by snaps. Bounding box about 372 x 169 x 402 mm.

Footprint is about 372 x 402 mm and height about 169 mm, which is a compact unit. I did not check it against a particular bench size or mounting, since the configurator has no bench model. It has no bolt-down or fixing feature.
Two drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm), one at cell (0,1) on level 0 and one at (0,1) on level 1, each sitting between the two touching bases of its storey.

requirements.requirement: Open faces closed and joints locked
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 12 solid caps; lockJoints added a joint bolt. check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey tower: four full hex bases (two per storey, side by side at (0,0) and (1,0)), with two notch drawer frames in the empty cells beside them, one per storey. Open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build reports no issues and a clear mesh check. Caveats: the build has 54 parts, above the modest count of about 40, because the caps and drawer frames add up; there are no props or drawer contents. I did not model strength, load or material suitability, since the configurator does not check those.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Two touching bases per storey now give notch sites. I'll join the second storey, then list the drawer-frame notch sites.

The tower now has two notch drawers, which meets the "at least two" requirement. Adding more would push past the modest part count, so I'll stop there. Next I'll cap the open faces, lock the joints, and run checks.
